title: FedSDR: Federated Self-Distillation with Rectification
claim: Mapping heterogeneous client data into the model's own understanding space smooths distribution boundaries, aligning clients, as shown empirically by embedding plots.
layout: 3 panels: top geometric sketch with legend, bottom two t-SNE scatters side by side
description: The top panel (a) is a geometric cartoon. A gray cloud of dots, the task dataset distribution, sits inside a green dashed box labeled Correct Data Space. An orange arrow points from the cloud to a pale orange ellipse, the innate knowledge distribution. A darker orange oval inside it is the distilled dataset distribution. A pink dashed box, the Model Understanding Space, overlaps the green box and encloses the ellipse. A legend on the right explains the colors and line styles. Below are two t-SNE scatter plots with many colored points, one color per client. Panel (b), Raw Data: Heterogeneous, shows distinct, separated clusters. Panel (c), Distilled: Aligned, shows the same colors mixed into a diffuse shared distribution. The eye goes first to the cartoon and then to the contrast between the two scatters.
caption: The Data Refinery Process. (a) Conceptual Illustration: FedSD leverages the model's Innate Knowledge Distribution as a universal manifold to re-map disjoint, client-specific raw data (gray) into a unified Model Understanding Space (red), transforming sharp data boundaries into a smoothed manifold. (b-c) Empirical Validation: t-SNE visualization on the Databricks Dolly-15K dataset confirms the "manifold flattening" effect, where self-distillation dissolves distinct client clusters into a shared, synchronized distribution to facilitate stable global aggregation.
abstract: Federated fine-tuning of Large Language Models faces severe statistical heterogeneity. However, existing model-level defenses often overlook the root cause: intrinsic data distribution mismatches. In this work, we first establish Federated Self-Distillation (FedSD) as a fundamental and potent strategy. By projecting client representations into a smoothed ``model-understanding space,'' FedSD alone serves as a universal booster, demonstrating superior performance over conventional algorithms. Despite its success, we identify a subtle trade-off termed the Rewrite Paradox -- unconstrained self-distillation can inadvertently increase hallucinations and redundancy. To refine this paradigm, we further propose FedSDR (Federated Self-Distillation with Rectification), the ultimate reinforced framework. It augments FedSD with a dual-stream mechanism: a local LoRA-S (Smoothing) branch to implicitly absorb heterogeneity via distilled data, and a parallel global LoRA-R (Rectification) branch anchored to raw data to enforce factual correctness. By selectively aggregating only LoRA-R, FedSDR yields a globally aligned and faithful model. Extensive experiments verify its superior performance.
